issues.detail: The Greek 'τυποι συνεβαινον' (typoi synebainon) means 'were types' or 'were patterns' (in the sense of being prototypes/shadows). The Vietnamese 'xảy ra như mẫu' translates to 'happened as a model/sample,' which slightly shifts the grammatical function from a predicate of 'these things' to an adverbial description of how they happened.

The Greek 'εγραφη δε προς νουθεσιαν ημων' (egraphe de pros nouthesian hēmōn) means 'were written for our admonition/exhortation.' The Vietnamese 'đã được chép để khuyên bảo chúng ta' captures the meaning well, but the Greek 'nouthesia' specifically implies a warning or exhortation, which is slightly broader than just 'khuyên bảo' (advice).
